title: The Shift to Remote Work
text:
Many companies now allow employees to work from home for part of the week. This arrangement, sometimes called hybrid work, has reduced commuting time for a large number of staff. Supporters argue that it improves concentration, whereas critics claim that it weakens team cohesion.

Employers are therefore revising their policies. Some have concluded that regular in-person meetings are essential, while others have moved most of their operations online. In other words, the debate concerns not whether remote work should exist, but how it should be structured.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what has hybrid work reduced for many staff?
According to the first paragraph, what do critics of remote work claim?
What can the reader infer about the debate described in the second paragraph?
options: Most people agree on whether remote work should exist.
The debate is about how remote work should be organised.
Employers have stopped revising their policies.
Critics have completely won the argument.

questions.text: Why does the writer use the phrase 'In other words'?
options: To restate the previous idea in simpler terms
To mark the end of the passage

vocabulary.definition: the sense of unity and connection within a group
travelling regularly between home and work
arranged in a planned and orderly way

paragraph_translations: Muchas empresas permiten ahora que los empleados trabajen desde casa parte de la semana. Este sistema, a veces llamado trabajo híbrido, ha reducido el tiempo de desplazamiento para un gran número de personal. Los partidarios sostienen que mejora la concentración, mientras que los críticos afirman que debilita la cohesión del equipo.

Por ello, las empresas están revisando sus políticas. Algunas han concluido que las reuniones presenciales periódicas son esenciales, mientras que otras han trasladado la mayor parte de sus operaciones a internet. En otras palabras, el debate no trata de si el teletrabajo debe existir, sino de cómo debe estructurarse.
